the inverted spectrum case asks whether two people could share functional roles while their color experience is swapped. Locke has the early version. Shoemaker makes the modern pressure test. (Locke, 1689; Shoemaker, 1982)

the case only works if same function plus same public language leaves phenomenal character open. Hardin presses from color structure. Hue, saturation, brightness, and opponent relations constrain what a color experience can be. (Hardin, 1988) Dennett presses the evidential criteria. If every use and discrimination is held fixed, it becomes unclear what evidence remains for the inversion. (Dennett, 1988)

the payoff for this cluster is narrow. Inverted spectrum is a stress test for [functionalism](/thoughts/functionalism). It asks whether functional sameness entails phenomenal sameness.
